appDesc.message: Trace a formula's inputs in Google Sheets: Ctrl+Shift+A, walk the referenced cells with ↑↓, across sheets. For financial models.

actionTitle.message: Scopion — open on the selected cell (Ctrl+Shift+A)

cmdToggle.message: Open Scopion on the selected cell (re-audit when already open)

obLead.message: It shows which cells a formula reads, and walks you through them. Three steps to the first trace:

obStep1.message: Open a Google Sheets spreadsheet (reload the tab if it was already open).

obStep2.message: Select a cell that contains a formula.

obStep3.message: Press Ctrl+Shift+A, or click the Scopion icon in the toolbar.

obReload.message: This spreadsheet was open before Scopion was installed. Reload the tab, then press Ctrl+Shift+A.

obConsentBody.message: The first trace asks you to sign in and grant read-only access to your spreadsheets. Scopion reads the sheet through the Google Sheets API to show values, named ranges and hidden sheets. It makes exactly one kind of change: when the walk enters a hidden sheet, Sheets unhides it, and Scopion hides it again when you close the panel — for that it asks for edit access separately, the first time it is needed; decline and it tells you which sheets to re-hide by hand. Nothing is sent anywhere except to Google's own API.

obKeyWalk.message: ↑ ↓  walk the references; the selection follows

obKeyDrill.message: →  make the highlighted cell the new origin

obKeyBack.message: ←  or  Backspace  go back one origin

obKeyStay.message: Enter  close and stay where the walk left you

obKeyReturn.message: Esc  or  OK  return to where you started and close

obLimit1.message: Excel files opened in Sheets (.xlsx) have no API data: references and jumps work, values show as —, and hidden sheets you walked into stay visible until you re-hide them.

obLimit2.message: OFFSET, INDEX and INDIRECT are resolved from literals and single-cell values; anything else is listed as unresolved, never dropped.

obLimit3.message: If Ctrl+Shift+A is taken by another extension, rebind it in Chrome's shortcut settings.
